scope: Management TLS provider SHA-256/HMAC state uses Charlotte erasing owners. The existing one-shot HMAC delegates to the same incremental implementation. No cipher, handshake, wire, deadline or capability change; no finding closure.
bundle_digest_algorithm: sha256 of UTF-8 JSON bundle_sha256 map, sorted keys and compact separators

qualification.retained_storage: Drop of original and cloned unfinished HMAC contexts covers two keyed SHA states each, five key lengths and six input lengths; checks initialized state words, buffer, buffer length and total length without inspecting padding or freed memory. Existing unfinished SHA checks remain.
qualification.vectors: Existing independent Python hashlib/hmac vectors: 16 SHA message lengths, seven HMAC key lengths; incremental HMAC and clones each cover every split of a 129-byte input. SHA forks preserve the original transcript.
qualification.interop: Independent Rustls/ring client and OpenSSL client authenticate the freestanding server engine. Native verified TLS covers both management interfaces.
static: strict Clippy for all service binaries on AArch64 and x86_64

limits: Pinned original provider driver contexts lacked an erasure policy in source; no runtime retained-storage reproduction of that original opaque provider was performed.
Retained-storage checks qualify initialized fields of the shared owner, not every provider/Rustls allocation or stack/register copy.
Rustls returned hash/tag, HKDF, traffic-key, transcript/parser copies and the connector TLS client Embassy contexts retain separate lifetimes.
Ordinary Drop cannot establish erasure after forced termination, allocator-history erasure, physical erasure, protected custody or remote cleanup.
Native management controls establish the executed finite workloads, not sustained flood fairness or all hardware qualification.
SEC-15 remains partial; finding counts and unresolved incident attributions are unchanged.
